I post this review as neutral as I can. I write this for those who are on the fence about getting this game and the pros and cons for getting this game.

While I do like submarines and love WWII games in general, I don't believe this to be the best submarine game on the market. I will however state that if you want to play a multiplayer submarine game with the ability for multiple people to be on the same submarine this game is the one for those scenarios. While I don't have much time in this game I do find it quite enjoyable to play with friends and while you can play alone, I would recommend that another game might be better and more developed than this game. Wolfpack is a good multiplayer game to sum it up nicely. 

Main gripe for this game being development status and hearing that development has stalled, I would say that that is a bummer but not a necessary deal breaker. If you want multiplayer as stated before than this is truly a one of a kind game and would absolutely recommend it if you have friends to enjoy it with. 

While this game will definitely never be the pinnacle of submarine gaming in the general sense, it is already a decent overall semi-simulation game. I say semi-simulation in a lose sense of that it is not a true open world, although at the time this is written it is stated that they will make it such but that has not yet been done. This still captures much of the difficulty that you would expect from a WWII submarine simulation game but in a much more skirmish style setup.

Another thing to consider is time, as you will need a lot. I personally have never been able to conduct multiple attacks on a convoy in a single sitting due to various reasons. While I could find time to do it the people I play with would also have to find that time as well. This is something that should be considered as a immersion factor but not necessary a deal breaker as I have still had a lot of fun just attacking once or twice before having to get off.

As a final overview, whether you spend your money on this game is up to you to decide. The community for this game is quite small and while I would love for it to grow in size, the decision to buy this game is in your hands. I hope that this was helpful for those who read it and that you can use this to make a decision for your self.

This game isn't easy or casual. Don't be afraid, don't be intimidated. If I can do it, you can do it.  You will read manuals and or watch videos at some point. At first it can be overwhelming but that changes fast, if you can follow instructions or use a checklist. 

You can play Singleplayer with Bots, or Coop with others (as a Crew member or on other Uboats as a Wolfpack). Depending on your station, you will turn wheels, flip switches, blow fuses and putting them back in, calculate torpedo solution, calculate course/position (do basic math).... You have to plan and think ahead. 

Example:
You don't simply run the Diesel Engine, like hold F to fix,... ohhh no. If the engine is not warm enough, and you just go full throttle, it will drown. Then you need to stop it, open all valves and blow out the water/diesel, close them and restart.  There are real laws of physics in this game. Electro Motors and Batteries if not handled correctly will blow fuses..... 

If you want to play as Captain and only shoot Torpedo, let the bots do all the other work and focus on the Target Solution, which isnt really difficult. You just need to be accurate. Bots can be turned on or off for specific stations. So you can make it 1,2, 3,... player. 
The video about the Navigation Station hurt my brain and I decided to let the Bots do the navigation for now ;) (update: wasn't that difficult after all. But the Bot doing the navigation looks so happy. I think I can't take that job away from him.)

After a steep learning curve and screaming at the blown fuse, because you forgot to put voltage on high again,  it feels extremly rewarding. Once you figured out any station, you will be proud of yourself and call your wife down to your basement, to tell her that you finally can charge both batteries, while running both engines, while maintaining ordered speed. She will make you a hot coco or hand over some divorce papers. Either way you will feel a sense of pride and accomplishment.

Wolfpack — это когда ты выпускник элитной морской школы в Кёнигсберге, а твои подчинённые — вчерашние фольксдойче из Судетской области, которые, кроме гор, ничего в своей жизни и не видели. А во флот попали из-за проблем со здоровьем — и именно под твоё командование.

Поход начинался штатно, пока конвой не показался на горизонте. Ежесекундно была скомандована команда на погружение. На удивление, падение лодки удалось стабилизировать, и она зависла на глубине 13 метров.

Не будем брать во внимание, что в этот момент дизеля были затоплены из-за того, что механик забыл их переключить. Началось движение: курс проложен, как и дистанция. Но вот незадача — с каждой минутой мы отдалялись от конвоя. Как выяснилось, механик спутал ход вперёд и назад, и лодка уже несколько минут пятилась, тратя драгоценный заряд батарей.

Но вот лодка была уже на острие атаки, конвой был как на ладони, и тут выяснилось, что навигатор не сумел рассчитать курс судов и их скорость. Приходилось пускать торпеды на глаз, исходя из имеющихся данных. Из трёх попала только одна — это уже был фурор! Экипаж ликовал до момента, пока всепроникающий АСДИК не начал бить по корпусу лодки в её поисках.

Собравшись в центральном отсеке, я с ужасом обнаружил, что батареи почти сели, и перспектива зависнуть на глубине без скорости была мне не в радость. Была отдана команда занять позиционное положение, чтобы хоть немного зарядить батареи. Вот тут-то нас и засёк эсминец, который и отправил нас на дно.

Ну что сказать — 10 необученных экипажей из 10.

Perfektes Konzept: Man steckt die falschen Leute in ein U-Boot, von denen eigentlich keiner weiß, was er tut. Am Ende sitzt man mit verschwitzten Männern in einer engen Blechdose, alle schreien sich gegenseitig an und jeder Befehl vom Kaleu wird je nach Stimmung umgesetzt – oder exakt falsch.

Der Kaleu selbst verschießt Torpedos nach dem Prinzip Glücksspiel. Die Trefferwahrscheinlichkeit liegt gefühlt unter der eines Lottogewinns, aber Hauptsache alle Torpedos sind irgendwann weg. Danach folgt konsequent der Frontalangriff mit der Deckkanone auf einen feindlichen Zerstörer. Ergebnis wie immer: Wir haben natürlich „gewonnen“.

Zusätzlich gibt es den Tauchgnom, der bei jeder sich bietenden Gelegenheit den Alarm drückt, egal ob nötig oder nicht. Spannung muss sein.

Unterm Strich ist das ein Spiel, das für gewisse Positionen eigentlich einen Mindestschulabschluss voraussetzt, den aber niemand mitbringt. Der Kaleu bräuchte mindestens Abi+, damit auch mal irgendwas trifft. Tauchmeister und Steuermann kommen mit Hauptschule durch. Maschinist sollten eher Realschulabschluss haben. Und der Kartenmann muss sich ein dreistündiges Fortbildungsvideo reinziehen, Mathe-LK gehabt haben und innerlich bereits mit seinem Leben abgeschlossen haben.
